title: Circular Motion
standard_text: Uniform circular motion: period and frequency, centripetal acceleration and centripetal force, and circular motion in vehicles, rides and orbits. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 12)
meta_desc: Free Physics 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): centripetal acceleration and centripetal force. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: a(c) = v² ÷ r, directed toward the centre.
key_sub: Centripetal force is the net force toward the centre.
body_html:
How to think about it

An object moving in a circle at constant speed is accelerating because its direction changes. The centripetal acceleration is ac = v² ÷ r = 4π²r ÷ T², toward the centre. Speed v = 2πr ÷ T.

The centripetal force Fc = mv² ÷ r is not a new force: it is the net force toward the centre, supplied by tension, friction, gravity or the normal force. Without it, the object would move off in a straight line (tangent).

Example

A 1.0 kg ball on a string moves at 4.0 m/s in a 2.0 m circle. What is the tension?

F = mv² ÷ r

Answer: 8.0 N

Example

If the string breaks, which way does the ball go?

Newton's first law

Answer: in a straight line along the tangent

Common mistakes

  • Thinking there is an outward 'centrifugal' force on the object.
  • Thinking constant speed means no acceleration.
  • Forgetting to square v.

faq.q: What supplies the centripetal force for a car on a flat curve?
faq.a: Friction between the tires and the road.

faq.q: Why do you feel lighter at the top of a roller-coaster loop?
faq.a: Less normal force is needed, since gravity supplies part of the centripetal force.
